criterionMeaning.houseEntry: No premature giant/trapped limb or Mary Ann conflation.
criterionMeaning.grownHouse: Clearly giant and one coherent body; exact window/chimney pose is separately recorded as selectedInstant.
criterionMeaning.cellar: Selected later waiting/floor-light instant, with no open bright lantern, wall-tunnel substitution or premature thieves. An earlier source-supported preparation can fail this selected-instant criterion without being globally unfaithful to the whole focal passage.

items.notes: Alice is a normal-sized kneeling child outside the intact cottage while the Rabbit points at her. No premature growth, trapped limb or Mary Ann conflation. The distant house is in perspective; no claim of an exact height. No clear lettering or body defect is visible.

Alice is an ordinary-sized child outside the intact cottage, reacting to the pointing Rabbit. No premature giant or trapped limb. The door plate has visible W. RABBIT-like lettering; the existing checker requested a retry.

The replacement retains a normal-sized seated child outside the cottage and the pointing Rabbit, with no premature growth or trapped limb. The plate is unreadable/blank. A small solid black square near the upper-right foliage is a visible image artifact; clearing the checker does not establish overall quality.

Alice reacts at ordinary human scale outside an intact cottage; no trapped giant limb or premature growth. Her face and proportions read older than in the first pair. A maze, ruins and oversized mushrooms add unrequested scenery. The plate is too small to confidently read; the automated check, rather than this inspection, reported lettering.

Alice remains a child-scale seated figure reacting to the Rabbit outside the house, with no premature growth. Oversized mushrooms, a maze and ruins remain additional scenery. Alice reads younger than the first attempt. The door plate appears blank at this resolution.

Child-scale Alice starts away from the pointing Rabbit outside an intact cottage; no premature growth or trapped limb. The Rabbit lacks the plan's hat, and mushrooms/stream add scenery. The plate appears blank; the narrow growth control passes without certifying every plan detail.

Alice moves away at child scale beside the intact cottage and pointing Rabbit. No premature growth or trapped limb. Added maze/ruin and mushrooms remain; the door plate is blank. Rabbit scale and cottage architecture vary across repeats.

Alice reacts to the Rabbit at ordinary human scale; the distant intact house does not contain a giant or trapped limb. Her proportions read older than the baseline child. The house has a red roof rather than the repeated slate design, and abundant colored mushrooms/stream add scenery. The narrow entry control passes.

Alice is clearly enormous relative to the door, table and chair, but two arms cluster at her head/door while a separate third sleeved arm enters through the opposite window. Neither visible boot follows the foot-up-chimney pose. The picture combines the competing poses and does not give one coherent body.

Alice clearly dwarfs the cramped room. Two legs extend toward the right, but a small skin-colored toe-like shape under the central hem makes the single-body reading uncertain. One hand remains around her head, and the window arm lies in front of the glazing rather than clearly outside. The feet press against the chimney face/hearth rather than clearly going up its flue. This does not establish the selected pose.

A clearly giant Alice has a readable torso, two arms and two legs. This passes only the declared giant/single-body check. Her hand holds the window frame instead of reaching outside, and a boot breaks into the chimney's side above the hearth rather than clearly going up the flue. The room and furniture are damaged; the mirror repeats her face. The selected arm/window/foot/chimney pose is not faithfully established.

Alice is enormous, with two readable arms, one raised leg and a folded lower leg; the body is coherent enough for the narrow giant/body criterion. The arm is in front of the window, one hand stays above her head and a boot presses on the door rather than entering the chimney. It does not reproduce the selected window/chimney instant.

A giant Alice has two arms and two legs in a readable, if strained, pose. Her left arm reaches the open window and the other remains around her head; the upper boot presses against the chimney exterior rather than clearly going up its flue. This passes giant size/single body only, not the requested spatial arrangement.

Alice is clearly giant, but a separate arm/hand extends through the window from beside a stockinged lower leg while two more arms attach to her torso. One of those arms reaches into the chimney, substituting a hand for the required foot. The body and chosen pose remain incoherent; the correction does not eliminate extra limbs.

The exposed lantern is brightly lit and Merryweather sits openly on a crate. This reads closer to earlier preparations than the selected later concealed waiting instant. No clear floor glint is distinguished. Arched passages are not proof of a dug wall tunnel. Crates carry extensive lettering.

The replacement has pale exposed lantern panes, but reflection versus emission is difficult to establish. Merryweather remains openly seated, and the later floor-light instant is not clearly readable. This could still depict earlier preparations; it is not an overall verdict on the entire focal passage. Extensive NAPOLEONS-like crate lettering remains.

Holmes holds an openly glowing lantern while additional corridor lamps are lit. The men are not consistently concealed; a uniformed man stands in the corridor. This contradicts the selected shuttered-lantern waiting instant. There is no definite dug wall breach; ordinary arched corridors should not be counted as one. Large crate lettering remains.

A bright flame is visible through the exposed lantern, alongside a line of light under a distant opening. The image retains the incompatible open lantern; the floor cue does not repair that contradiction. Men remain partly exposed and extensive crate lettering persists.

Holmes holds a visibly glowing open lantern while a line of light appears low at the back, again mixing the selected late floor-light cue with an unshuttered lamp. Three men are visible; a fourth could be concealed and is not automatically counted missing. Crate lettering and a lower-right signature are clear.

The men wait among crates, and no open handheld lantern is visible. Small bright objects and pooled light at the rear floor could be lamps/candles or the intended glint; the image does not resolve that origin. It therefore does not clearly establish the selected instant. No definite dug wall breach or thieves appear; faint crate lettering remains.

No open lantern is visible, but the men are openly seated and the low left floor light is too ambiguous to establish the later first-glint instant. It can read as earlier waiting/preparations. The arches do not establish a dug wall breach. Crate lettering remains.

A bright exposed lantern illuminates the floor while Merryweather and Jones sit openly. A shadowy additional head/figure appears behind Holmes, separate from the four foreground men. The picture does not match the selected concealed waiting instant; large crate lettering remains.

The lantern is visibly bright and the men sit openly; light also enters through a low arched wall opening rather than a clearly distinguishable floor glint. This fails the selected late-instant criterion. A constructed arch alone cannot prove it depicts the thieves' dug tunnel. Crate lettering remains.

The lantern appears unlit, but the light enters from a small low wall opening, not a clear gap between floor flags. Five distinct men are visible rather than the selected four. Crate lettering and a lower-right signature remain. The chosen late instant is not established.

The glass lantern beside Holmes visibly glows while a separate light patch sits at the distant floor. This keeps the open-lantern conflict with the selected waiting instant. The men are partly screened by crates; no definite thieves or dug wall breach are visible. Crate lettering remains.

Holmes's lantern is mostly dark, with a small warm pane that could be reflection or emission. Low light at the far left appears to come from a vertical wall/door gap rather than a clearly readable first glint between floor flags. Several men remain exposed. The exact source instant is uncertain; the picture is not a confirmed pass. Crate lettering persists.
